# 🏴 dsh-gitea
🇬🇧 **English** | 🇨🇳 中文 | 🇷🇺 Русский
**Gitea/Forgejo, driven from your DeepSeek Harness session.**
Main repo on pvlb.dev/dsh-plugins/dsh-gitea
96 first-class tools · preset-switchable surface · settings page · live Git status chip
Install · Configure · The toolset · Safety · Development · npm
## What it is

`dsh-gitea` connects a DeepSeek Harness session to your own Gitea or Forgejo
instance: the agent get

s 96 first-class, schema-declared tools for issues, pull
requests, reviews, CI, releases and reposit

ories (by default through the 2-tool
`dispatcher`, which serves each operation's schema on demand),

and you get a
**Settings → Gitea** page plus a **Git status chip** in the session header.
Nothing is

scraped from a web page — every call is a typed tool over the REST
API, with your token resolved fr

om DSH credentials at call time.
Read a PR, review it, rebase it, watch its CI, tag the release and

file the
follow-up issue without leaving the chat.

*A fork of GooDAnDReaDY/dsh-gitea
(MIT) — see Built on upstream for what this fork adds.*
## What you can do with it

- **Plan the work.** File one issue or fifty, with labels (by name *or* id),
an assignee and a miles

tone in a single call; check for duplicates and lint
the Definition of Done first; walk the chronolo

gical timeline before you
answer; bulk-retag a backlog from a dry run you approved.
- **Read and cha

nge code with context.** Browse branches, tags, files, commits
and diffs; search code locally when t

he forge API cannot; compare two refs
before you merge them.
- **Review like a maintainer.** Inline

comments with one-click suggestions,
approve or request changes, and get a rule-based risk summary —

areas
touched, tests, migrations, merge state — plus a review inbox and reviewer
suggestions from `

CODEOWNERS` and commit history.
- **Merge safely.** A merge gate that checks description, conflicts,

approval, tests and migrations; auto-merge only when the gate is green;
stacked-PR chains with reba

se helpers; conflict analysis that names the
category of every hunk and can apply resolutions. Destr

uctive steps need
`confirm: true`; the rest are dry runs first.
- **Ship it.** Conventional-Commits

release planning, semver validation,
changelog drafts, tags, releases, CI run inspection with log ro

ot-cause
analysis, and the package registry (npm, PyPI, OCI, generic) with
ready-to-paste client con

fig.
- **Run the project.** Health reports, a daily triage digest, a duty-officer
snapshot, schedule

d read-only checks, branch protection, deploy keys, a
security audit, and webhooks you can replay of

fline.
- **Work where the repo lives.** Git worktrees for isolated branches, a
commit graph in the U

I, and an issue → branch → worktree → PR flow that
keeps the issue and the code in sync.
*The Git drawer — repository link, branch, sync state, changes and recent commits.*
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.x` — the `0.2.0` and `0.2.1` prerelease lines are both
in the package's peer

range.
- Node.js 20 or newer.
- `pnpm` that DSH can execute — Plugin Manager shells out to it for p

rofile
installs.
- `git` on the DSH host for the install straight from the repository.
- A Gitea or

Forgejo instance reachable over HTTPS from the DSH host, plus an
API token for it.

blished to the public npm registry as

The command adds `dsh-gitea` to the profile and selects its bundle — the package
declares `dsh.bundl

e`, so the plugin row is enabled without a separate Plugin
Manager step. There is no checkout to boo

the plugin row is enabled without a separate Plugin
Manager step. There is no checkout to bootstrap.

DSH applies the new profile by itself — in the web profile HMR watches the
bundle list; on a profile

without HMR, restart the DSH service. Refresh the
browser tab afterwards.

The `.git` suffix is what makes pnpm treat the URL as a git repository. Without
it the URL is fetche

d as a tarball and the install fails with
`ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_HTTP_STATUS … 404`.

Either way the package is self-contained — `lib/index.js` plus
`cordis.patch.yml` — and its DSH peer
s come from the profile.
## Configure
Two settings are all that matter; the rest of the page can stay default.

1. **Instance URL.** Open **Settings → Gitea** — or **Plugins → dsh-gitea →
Configure** — and set `b

aseUrl`, for example `https://git.example.com`.
2. **Token.** In Forgejo/Gitea open **Settings → App

lications → Generate token**
with the repository, issue and pull-request scopes (`read:user` covers

`gitea_whoami`). Then store the secret in DSH credentials under the name the
form expects — `GITEA_T
OKEN`, unless you changed `tokenEnv`.

The store is the hidden file `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`; its top level is
`version: 1`, then `record
s:` and `refs:`. Add the name under `refs:`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

If the file already exists, merge that one line into its `refs:` block and
leave the rest alone. A n

ew file needs `version: 1` followed by the block
above. Other DSH key editors write to the same stor

e, so this file is simply
the direct route for a name nothing else manages.

The settings form takes the credential **name**, never the token — a token-shaped
value is refused.

DSH's credential store reloads this file on change and resolves
the secret per call, so a new or rot

ated token applies to the next tool call
without a restart.

Optional: set `defaultOwner` and `defaultRepo` so tools that omit `owner`/`repo`
fall back to your u

efaultOwner` and `defaultRepo` so tools that omit `owner`/`repo`
fall back to your usual repository.
### Tool surface — keep the payload small

Every registered tool's schema is bound into every request, so the plugin has a
preset switch. **The

default is `dispatcher`** (since 0.8.9): two meta-tools that
keep all 96 operations reachable while

the always-on payload stays ~9 KB
